label: Subject Alternative Name (SAN)
type: the X.509 certificate extension Couchbase Server requires a node certificate to use to identify its node (`subjectAltName = DNS:node2.cb.com`), and one of the places a CLIENT certificate can carry the username Couchbase authenticates as. The IETF-sanctioned replacement for the Subject Common Name.
evidence: The node certificate for each server in the cluster must specify its node name as a Subject Alternative Name.
The `DNS` name, provided as a Subject Alternative Name for the certificate.
The following `subjectAltName` statement allows an email address to be specified as the basis for the username.
Cannot validate certificate for _<ip-address>_ because it doesn't contain any IP SANs
note: Recurs across the reference page, two configuration procedures and a troubleshooting page - and it is the troubleshooting page that earns it a record, because the error text 'doesn't contain any IP SANs' is the form in which an administrator actually meets this concept. Round 26's cert: additions are the strongest counter-example to the round's own hypothesis that the security vocabulary was already complete: the tls:/cert: families were built from reference material and were missing both certificate fields that node and client identity are actually keyed on.
relates_to_competency_question: What must a node's certificate contain for the cluster to accept it?
